entries.name: CreateFrame

returns.Name: frame
returns.Type: Frame or another creatable frame type

notes: An omitted name creates an anonymous object; a supplied name exposes it globally.
The parent is a frame object or nil, not a string containing its name.
The template argument accepts comma-separated virtual XML template names. Inherited OnLoad handlers run during creation.
Frame objects are retained by the client; do not repeatedly create them expecting garbage collection.
limitations: The list of accepted frame types is not enumerated here. XML declarations alone do not prove that a type can be created by addons.
This contract does not grant access to protected behavior during combat.

entries.name: hooksecurefunc
notes: Installs a post-hook on a named function in the supplied table, or in the global table when the table is omitted.
The hook receives the original arguments after the original call. Hook return values are discarded; the original function's return values are preserved.
Repeated installations add hooks. Removing them requires reloading the UI.
Previously retained function references, including XML-held references, may not observe the replacement.
limitations: A secure post-hook does not make the hook body secure or authorize protected calls.

entries.name: issecurevariable
notes: Inspects a named table value; omitting the table selects the global environment. It cannot inspect a local variable.
Numeric names are converted to strings. Other key types are not supported.
Missing values are secure. An __index lookup can affect a check when the direct value is nil.
The second result identifies the tainting addon, is empty for macro taint, or is nil for a secure value.
limitations: A secure value does not prove that the current execution path is secure.

entries.name: issecure
notes: Reports whether the current execution path is secure. The calling path matters; the identity of a function alone is insufficient.
limitations: Calling this function does not change the security of the execution path.

migrations.name: UnitAura
notes: The replacement returns a nullable AuraData structure instead of the legacy positional tuple. Update consumers of the returned values rather than performing only a function-name substitution.

For the selected target build, inspect the replacement's generated contract and AuraData fields. Aura-access and secret-value restrictions can prevent legacy filtering, comparisons, or arithmetic from remaining valid.
Lifecycle annotations come from community documentation, not an inference from missing entries in the generated API catalog.
